subject: Trial qualification & prompt/log ingest - next steps (ChronoTech)
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Reynolds <ava.reynolds@chronotech.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Trial qualification & prompt/log ingest - next steps (ChronoTech)

Hi Ava / Michael —

Thanks again for the demo and the productive discussion this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment for the 3-week evaluation trial: 

High-level success criteria (what ChronoTech will measure):
- Quality: >= 85% pass rate on your 200-shot prompt set (business-critical QA list)
- Latency: p95 generation < 600ms for 512-token requests in our US region
- Cost: projected per-inference unit at or below your budget target (we'll estimate once we receive sample logs)
- Reliability: no more than 1 incident impacting throughput during the trial window

What we need from your side to run the trial and the eval:
1) Prompt set and example logs (anonymized): a CSV or JSONL with columns for prompt, expected output/scrubbed label, context tokens, and sample model responses where available. See the schema in the attached stub.
2) Priority evaluation buckets: which prompt groups are must-pass vs exploratory (label as critical / optional).
3) Ownership & timing: who on your team will provide the data and the final sign-off?

Redwood's deliverables / plan:
- Ingest prompts/logs, run an initial quality sweep and generate an evaluation plan by day 3 after data receipt.
- Provide a shared Drive folder with intermediate artifacts, model variants tested, and a simple dashboard for quality/latency/cost.
- Run canary rollouts and keep a dedicated channel with your team for rapid adjustments.

Proposed timeline (adjustable):
- By EOD Tue (2026-06-22): ChronoTech shares prompt/log samples and marks critical buckets.
- Wed–Fri (2026-06-23 to 06-25): Redwood ingests data, runs baseline evals, returns results + suggested model/quantization pairings.
- Week of 06-28: Trial live for tech validation; continuous monitoring and checkpoint call mid-week.

Attachments included (stubs): chronotech_trial_scope_v1.pdf (scope), prompt_log_schema.csv (schema)

Owners:
- ChronoTech data: Ava Reynolds (will coordinate uploads)
- Redwood trial lead: Sofia Ivanova
- Redwood eval & prompts: Jordan Blake and Marissa Cole

Next steps: please confirm who will upload the files and whether ChronoTech needs an S3 share or a Drive folder. If the timeline looks tight, tell us which dates to shift.

Thanks —
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova

Subject: Re: Trial qualification & prompt/log ingest - next steps (ChronoTech)

Hi Sofia —

Great summary, thanks. We're aligned on the success metrics listed. Quick answers and what we'll upload: 

1) Files: I'll upload a zipped collection to the shared Drive by EOD Tue (2026-06-22):
   - prompt_log_sample_200.csv (we'll redact PII; columns follow your schema)
   - expected_labels_200.csv (human-verified labels for critical prompts)
   - service_response_snippets.jsonl (sample model outputs from our legacy system)

2) Priority buckets: we'll tag ~50 prompts as CRITICAL (billing, cancellation flows, legal responses), 100 as STANDARD, rest as EXPERIMENTAL.

3) Ownership: I'll be the owner for uploads and sign-off; Michael Chu (cc'd) will handle legal redaction if needed.

Constraints:
- We cannot share raw customer IDs; everything will be anonymized.
- Our logs are UTC timestamps; include mapping note if you need timezone conversions.

We attached a small prompt_log_schema.csv to this reply that mirrors your stub but with a few ChronoTech-specific fields (tenant_hint, call_type). Let us know if you need the schema adjusted.

Thanks —
Ava

Sofia / Marissa —

Thanks — I reviewed Ava's schema and the notes. Quick internal checklist before ingest: 
- Confirm anonymization fields (Ava: please confirm tenant_hint is non-PII).
- Map ChronoTech columns to Redwood eval pipeline: prompt_text -> source_prompt, expected_label -> gold_label, service_response_snippets -> baseline_resp.
- Generate a sampling plan: we'll hold back 20% of each bucket for blind evaluation.
- Propose models to test: Mistral-7B-quant (fast baseline), Llama-2-13B-ptq (quality), Redwood-mix-13B-if (balanced).

I'll prepare the Redwood_probe_checklist.xlsx and an onboarding README for their folder. Plan to start ingestion Wed morning once files are uploaded.

Marissa: can you own the label-coverage report and the initial eval dashboard?

-Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior ML Ops, Redwood Inference
